title: Ancient Egypt in One Level
objective: After this level you can describe the Old, Middle and New Kingdoms and roughly when each flourished.
summary: Ancient Egypt lasted about 3,000 years. Its three great kingdoms, Old, Middle and New, were separated by Intermediate Periods when the land split.

cards.headline: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the Great Pyramid.
cards.body: That’s how long ancient Egypt lasted. So how do you keep a story that long straight in your head? Start with the big shape.

events.label: Upper and Lower Egypt become one kingdom
Old Kingdom: the age of the great pyramids
New Kingdom: Egypt becomes an empire
Egypt becomes a province of Rome

cards.headline: Peaks and valleys
cards.body: Egypt’s story isn’t one smooth climb. Between the three kingdoms came the First, Second and Third Intermediate Periods, when the country split apart, often into local rule in Upper and Lower Egypt. Each time, the land was eventually pulled back together and a new great age began. Picture a mountain range: historians named the peaks Old, Middle and New. The valleys got the less glamorous name “Intermediate.”

mascot.line: Don’t sweat the dates. Remember the rhythm: kingdom, split, kingdom, split, kingdom.

cards.context: Count from the first kings, around 3100 to 3000 BCE, to 30 BCE, when Egypt became a province of Rome. That’s one civilization running for longer than the time between Cleopatra and you. Why it lasted so long is this chapter’s story, and it starts with a river.

cards.headline: Ancient Egypt: the big picture
learned: Old, Middle and New Kingdoms, in that order
Intermediate Periods: times when the land split
Egypt became a Roman province in 30 BCE

questions.prompt: Which list puts ancient Egypt’s three great kingdoms in order, earliest first?
questions.explanation: Old Kingdom from about 2686 BCE, Middle Kingdom from about 2055 BCE, New Kingdom from about 1550 BCE.

questions.prompt: What happened in Egypt during its “Intermediate Periods”?

options.label: The country split, often into local rule
Egypt fought long wars against Rome
options.rationale: Rome arrived only at the very end.

options.label: The Nile stopped flooding for a century
options.rationale: The periods are about politics, not the river.

options.label: Kings moved the capital to Greece

questions.explanation: Between the kingdoms, central power broke down and the land was divided until it was reunited.

questions.prompt: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid. What does that show?

options.label: Cleopatra ordered the Great Pyramid built
options.rationale: It was over two thousand years old in her day.

options.label: Ancient Egypt lasted a remarkably long time
The Great Pyramid is younger than people think
options.rationale: It is far older than Cleopatra.

options.label: The Moon landing was in ancient times

questions.explanation: Egyptian civilization ran for about 3,000 years, so even Cleopatra was a latecomer to it.
